correctness.rationale: For the unilateral shift S with Gamma_j=I, Lambda_1=I+S and Lambda_j=S^j-S^{j-1}, the finite mixed sums telescope exactly to I+S^N. The scalar quadratic sums tend to ||f||^2 because <S^Nf,f> tends to zero by an l2 tail estimate, satisfying the printed Parseval condition. The vector sums f+S^Nf cannot converge in norm for nonzero f because S is an isometry and S^Nf converges weakly to zero. Under two g-Bessel assumptions, bounded analysis/synthesis operators give unconditional convergence and the quadratic lower bound makes the resulting bounded self-adjoint operator positive and invertible.

value.rationale: The invalid step is foundational: it is what turns the scalar definition into the reconstruction operator. The counterexample already occurs in the Parseval case using bounded operators, and the g-Bessel repair identifies a standard safe regime. This is a substantive domain-of-validity correction.

final_claim: Under the literal scalar definition of a bi-g-frame, a Parseval pair can have a mixed series \(\sum_j\Gamma_j^*\Lambda_jf\) that fails to converge in norm for every nonzero \(f\); simultaneous g-Bessel hypotheses restore unconditional convergence and the standard positive-invertible mixed operator.
limitations: The simultaneous g-Bessel condition is sufficient, not claimed necessary.
Only the general well-definedness assertion at the printed level of generality is refuted.
